articles.title: Suraksha insurance scheme approved for 2026/27 academic year with expanded coverage
articles.text:
The Cabinet of Ministers has granted approval to implement the “Suraksha” Student Insurance Scheme for the 2026/27 operational year, featuring a significantly expanded array of medical and accidental coverage benefits for students across Sri Lanka.
The agreement between the Ministry of Education, Higher Education, and Vocational Education and Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation General Limited will run for the period from September 1, 2026, to August 31, 2027.
The scheme covers all students enrolled in government schools, government-approved private schools, Pirivenas, and assisted special education schools, Cabinet Spokesperson Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said.
Key amendments and enhanced benefits include:
Hearing Aid Repairs: Allowances up to LKR 75,000 for the repair of hearing accessories and related service charges.
Chronic Illness Medication: Allowances up to LKR 20,000 for students taking long-term medications for Chronic Kidney Disease and Chronic Inflammatory Arthritis.
Expanded Diagnostic Testing: Coverage up to LKR 20,000 for specialized diagnostic screenings, including Skin Cancer, Post-transplant Lymphoproliferative Disorder (PTLD), Osteoporosis, Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV.
Cancer and Critical Care Support: Reclassification of critical illness coverage to encompass “Cancer Treatment and related Testing”, as well as covering costs for PET Scans and major neurosurgeries necessitated by emergency accidents.
Student Safety Coverage: An emergency benefit of LKR 100,000 in the event of a tragic accidental death during school-organized activities—such as sports meets or educational trips—whether held on or off school grounds.
The proposal was presented to the Cabinet by the Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education, and Vocational Education.
articles.summary: The Cabinet of Ministers has granted approval to implement the “Suraksha” Student Insurance Scheme for the 2026/27 operational year, featuring a significantly expanded array of medical and accidental coverage benefits for students across Sri Lanka.

articles.title: DIMO selected to supply 200 vehicles to Sri Lanka Police
articles.text:
The Cabinet of Ministers has granted approval for the Sri Lanka Police to purchase 200 imported single-cab vehicles from the local market to support and enhance official police operations across the island.
The approval follows a decision made during the Cabinet meeting held on February 23, 2026.
To execute the procurement, tenders were called under the national competitive bidding procedure, attracting a total of seven bids from local suppliers, Cabinet Spokesperson Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said.
Upon thorough evaluation by the High-Level Procurement Committee, M/s Diesel and Motor Engineering PLC (DIMO) was selected as the substantially responsive lowest bidder, he said.
Under the approved proposal, which was submitted by the Minister of Public Security and Parliamentary Affairs, the Sri Lanka Police will acquire 200 TATA Yodha Single-Cab Pickups at a cost of Rs. 4,785,000 per unit (excluding VAT), the government said.

articles.title: Premium International Injectable advances pharmaceutical manufacturing ambitions in Sri Lanka
articles.text:
Premium International Injectable (Private) Limited is advancing the development of its pharmaceutical manufacturing facility in Sri Lanka, marking a significant step in the company’s commitment to strengthening local manufacturing capabilities and establishing a foundation for future growth in the country’s pharmaceutical sector.
The state-of-the-art facility, which is being developed to European standards within a Board of Investment (BOI) zone, is intended to support the manufacture of biotechnology-based insulin and generic Small Volume Parenteral (SVP) products. The plant is also geared to receive EU GMP certification, which is issued by National Competent Authorities (NCAs) within European Union member states. The project reflects the company’s ambition to establish a long-term manufacturing presence in Sri Lanka while exploring opportunities to expand its production capabilities in response to market requirements.
The visit by Hon. Minister of Health D.r Nalinda Jayatissa provided an opportunity to review the facility’s development and highlight the company’s plans for pharmaceutical manufacturing in Sri Lanka. It also provided an opportunity to discuss the role of private-sector investment in developing local manufacturing capabilities and strengthening the country’s pharmaceutical industry.
Thushira Raddella, Managing Director & CEO of Premium International Injectable (Private) Limited said, “Our investment in this facility reflects our long-term commitment to Sri Lanka and our confidence in the opportunities available within the country’s pharmaceutical manufacturing sector. We are focused on progressing the project towards completion and establishing a strong foundation for future growth. Beyond the current facility, we see opportunities to explore additional product strengths, doses and formulations in response to market requirements, while building strategic relationships that can support the next phase of our development.”
The facility’s planned focus on biotechnology-based insulin and generic SVP products represents an opportunity to develop specialised pharmaceutical manufacturing capabilities locally. Insulin manufacturing involves specific biotechnology and production requirements, while SVP products encompass injectable medicines administered in relatively small volumes. Both areas require appropriate manufacturing infrastructure, robust quality systems and compliance with applicable regulatory requirements.
The development of local pharmaceutical manufacturing capabilities has the potential to contribute to the resilience of medicine supply chains, broaden the country’s industrial capabilities and create opportunities for skills development and collaboration across the healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors.
Hon. Minister of Health Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said, “Developing pharmaceutical manufacturing capabilities in Sri Lanka presents an opportunity to strengthen medicine supply resilience and support the country’s healthcare sector. Such initiatives must be underpinned by robust quality standards, regulatory compliance and collaboration between the public and private sectors.”
Premium International Injectable is also engaging with relevant institutional and industry stakeholders, including the State Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing Corporation (SPMC), where applicable, as it advances its manufacturing plans. Such engagement provides an opportunity to explore areas of mutual interest and understand the requirements and opportunities within Sri Lanka’s pharmaceutical manufacturing landscape.
The company’s longer-term vision extends beyond the current facility. Subject to market demand, technical feasibility and the relevant regulatory requirements, it intends to explore opportunities to introduce additional product strengths, doses and formulations. This approach would allow the company to assess future manufacturing opportunities in line with evolving healthcare needs and the commercial requirements of the local market.
As the project progresses towards completion, Premium International Injectable is also open to discussions with potential investors, strategic partners, suppliers and other businesses interested in contributing to the development of pharmaceutical manufacturing in Sri Lanka. These opportunities could support future expansion, strengthen business relationships and create a broader platform for collaboration within the sector.
For Premium International Injectable, the facility represents the foundation of a longer-term commitment to Sri Lanka. By progressing its manufacturing ambitions and exploring opportunities for future development, the company aims to establish itself as a credible participant in the country’s pharmaceutical industry while contributing to the continued development of local manufacturing capabilities.
articles.summary: Premium International Injectable (Private) Limited is advancing the development of its pharmaceutical manufacturing facility in Sri Lanka, marking a significant step in the company’s commitment to strengthening local manufacturing capabilities and establishing a foundation for future growth in the country’s pharmaceutical sector.

articles.title: G.L. Peiris questioned by Bribery Commission over Shangri-La Hotel investment
articles.text:
Former Foreign Minister Prof. G.L. Peiris has revealed that he was questioned by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) over the circumstances surrounding the Shangri-La Hotel investment in Sri Lanka.
Explaining his involvement, Peiris said he assumed duties as Foreign Minister on April 23, 2010, several months after the end of the civil war, when Sri Lanka was facing significant economic challenges and struggling to attract foreign investment.
He said representatives of the internationally renowned Shangri-La hotel chain had expressed interest in exploring opportunities to establish a hotel in Sri Lanka and sought the government’s response to a proposed visit.
Peiris said he referred the matter to then-President Mahinda Rajapaksa, as he believed the decision required approval at the highest level.
According to Peiris, Rajapaksa welcomed the proposal and instructed him to encourage the investors to visit Sri Lanka, highlighting the improved security environment following the end of the war.
The former minister said promoting tourism was among the responsibilities assigned to him through an extraordinary gazette notification issued after he assumed office.
He said the government had encouraged the investment because it was expected to attract high-spending international tourists and strengthen investor confidence in Sri Lanka.
Peiris also argued that the arrival of Shangri-La helped create confidence among other international hotel operators, referring to subsequent developments, including the ITC Ratnadipa Hotel in Colombo.
He said the Colombo area had undergone significant development since 2010, with new hotels, roads and other infrastructure.
Peiris stressed that he had not been accused of wrongdoing in connection with the matter.
He said the Bribery Commission had summoned him solely to obtain information about the circumstances surrounding the investment and the government’s involvement at the time.
articles.summary: Former Foreign Minister Prof. G.L. Peiris has revealed that he was questioned by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) over the circumstances surrounding the Shangri-La Hotel investment in Sri Lanka. Peiris also argued that the arrival of Shangri-La helped create confidence among other international hotel operators, referring to subsequent developments, including the ITC Ratnadipa Hotel in Colombo.

articles.title: Supreme Court begins hearing petitions against anti-terrorism Bill
articles.text:
The Supreme Court has begun hearing petitions challenging the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill presented to Parliament.
A three-judge bench comprising Chief Justice Preethi Padman Surasena and Justices Achala Wengappuli and Sampath Abeykoon is hearing the petitions.
Around 25 petitions have been filed, arguing that certain provisions of the proposed legislation violate fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution.
The petitioners have urged the court to rule that the disputed provisions require approval by a two-thirds majority in Parliament and a referendum to be enacted.

articles.title: Sajith proposes special task force, wildlife hospital to protect Sri Lanka’s remaining tuskers
articles.text:
Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has proposed establishing a special task force to protect Sri Lanka’s remaining tuskers, alongside a dedicated wildlife hospital, modern veterinary facilities and a rapid-response unit to handle emergencies involving injured elephants.
Speaking in Parliament on Tuesday (20), Premadasa said Sri Lanka needed a stronger wildlife protection and emergency treatment system to prevent further losses of iconic tuskers following the death of Kavanthissa.
He proposed establishing a special elephant protection task force with the involvement of experienced wildlife officers, including Chathura Gunaratne and the investigation team led by Olugala, who were involved in an arrest connected to the Kavanthissa incident.
Premadasa said their expertise should be utilised to strengthen efforts to protect endangered tuskers and combat crimes involving elephants.
He also called for the establishment of a dedicated wildlife hospital equipped to treat seriously injured wild animals, particularly elephants requiring specialised medical attention.
The Opposition Leader said modern diagnostic equipment, mobile laboratory facilities, emergency treatment units and a rapid-response mechanism were urgently needed to improve the chances of saving injured wildlife.
He offered the opposition’s support in establishing such facilities, including assistance in securing foreign funding and other resources.
Premadasa also proposed involving foreign veterinary specialists in complex cases and strengthening cooperation between wildlife authorities, universities and other relevant institutions.
Highlighting shortages of wildlife veterinarians and other trained personnel, he urged the government to strengthen staffing and medical resources within the Department of Wildlife Conservation.
He further proposed including environmental organisations and civil society representatives in the expert committee appointed by the government to investigate Kavanthissa’s death, arguing that their participation would improve transparency and accountability.
Premadasa said lessons from the deaths of Kavanthissa, Bhathiya and Thekka Raja should be used to develop better treatment procedures and emergency response systems.
He stressed that protecting Sri Lanka’s remaining tuskers required practical reforms, improved veterinary capacity and coordinated action rather than responses only after an elephant had died.
articles.summary: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has proposed establishing a special task force to protect Sri Lanka’s remaining tuskers, alongside a dedicated wildlife hospital, modern veterinary facilities and a rapid-response unit to handle emergencies involving injured elephants.

The committee will be chaired by the Deputy Chairperson of Committees and will be responsible for implementing, monitoring and providing leadership for Parliament’s role in the national anti-corruption initiative.
The 12 MPs named to serve on the committee are:
* Harshana Nanayakkara
* Sunil Watagala
* Kaushalya Ariyarathne
* J. C. Alawathuwala
* Anuradha Jayaratne
* Shanakiyan Rasamanickam
* Oshani Umanga
* Prageeth Madhuranga
* Chandima Hettiarachchi
* Dharmapriya Wijesinghe
* Devananda Suraweera
* M. Nizam Kariapper
Together with the Deputy Chairperson of Committees, the committee comprises 13 members.
The committee is expected to coordinate parliamentary efforts to implement the National Anti-Corruption Action Plan over the 2025–2029 period.

articles.title: Australian MP Helen Haines loses leg after car attack — media
articles.text:
An Australian lawmaker struck by a car in an apparently deliberate attack on Monday has lost one of her legs, local media reported, citing sources.
Independent MP Helen Haines underwent surgery overnight after suffering what were described as critical injuries in the incident, with national broadcaster ABC and the daily Sydney Morning Herald reported on Tuesday that one leg had been amputated.
Counterterrorism investigators have joined a police probe into the incident, which occurred outside Haines’ constituency office in Wangaratta, northeast of the Victorian capital, Melbourne.
What do we know about the suspected attack on Haines? Haines, 65, was hit by an SUV, which police said was a white Toyota, outside her office. She suffered serious injuries, particularly to her lower body.
ABC cited witnesses as saying they heard a bang and then saw a woman pinned between two cars.
The driver, described as a 43-year-old man, has been arrested, according to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.
Albanese said early investigations suggested the driver made a U-turn before hitting Haines as she was loading or unloading items at the trunk of her car.
“This wasn’t an accident. There was a deliberate act, it would appear,” he told ABC.
Local barber ran to assist
Local barber Ricky Jeffries, whose shop is next to Haines’ office, has been widely hailed as a hero after he ran to pull the driver out of the car and restrained him until police arrived.
Jeffries downplayed his role, despite having intervened in what could have been a highly dangerous situation, as the man had a knife in the car.
“He [the driver] did have a knife. He didn’t ​pull it ‌out. I just wasn’t comfortable with his movements, and so I basically just took it out of his pocket and threw it away,” he said.
Jefferies said he then held the man down until ‌police arrived.
“I just leant over him and once he was on the ground and ‌he was ​no longer a threat, I just stood with him and I told him that he can’t leave,” he said.
Jefferies told journalists his first thought had been: “My wife would be disappointed if I’m injured.”
“The other people here were just, they did so much more than me … they deserve the credit,” he added.
Political violence on the rise: PM Albanese
Albanese said it was too early to speculate about the possible motive behind the suspected attack, but pointed to rising political violence.
“The temperature has increased in recent times,” Albanese added, “I’ve expressed that concern to people in the media.”
Ben Carroll, the state premier for Victoria where Wangaratta is located, said he was “appalled” by the attack, adding: “I know how devastating this will be for the Wangaratta community and all those who Helen represents.”
At a separate press conference, Albanese said everyone was “praying for her full recovery.”
Although it has not yet been established whether the incident was deliberate, there has been an increase in threats and harassment targeting lawmakers and other senior public officials in Australia and elsewhere in recent years.
Haines had worked as a nurse and a midwife before entering parliament in 2019. She is known for her stance on stronger climate action. (DW)
articles.summary: An Australian lawmaker struck by a car in an apparently deliberate attack on Monday has lost one of her legs, local media reported, citing sources. Independent MP Helen Haines underwent surgery overnight after suffering what were described as critical injuries in the incident, with national broadcaster ABC and the daily Sydney Morning Herald reported on Tuesday that one leg had been amputated.

articles.text:

Activists are also urging authorities to take stronger action to prevent similar incidents and ensure the long-term protection of the country’s elephant population.

articles.title: Viral video of woman threatening police officers dates back to 2024, police clarify
articles.text:
Sri Lanka Police have clarified that a video circulating on social media showing a woman allegedly threatening two police officers in Gandara relates to an incident that occurred on January 28, 2024.
According to the Police Media Division, the woman was arrested on the same day for allegedly verbally abusing and threatening a police sergeant, as well as threatening and assaulting a female police sergeant, causing injuries.
She also faced charges of reckless driving and failing to keep to the left side of the road.
The suspect was produced before the Kotavila Magistrate’s Court, where her driving licence was suspended. She was subsequently released on personal bail of Rs. 200,000.
Police said the woman pleaded not guilty when the case was taken up on March 26, 2024, and legal proceedings have continued.
However, investigations have since revealed that the accused had travelled overseas without informing the court.
As a result, the trial is proceeding in her absence under Section 192(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, with the proceedings remaining binding on the accused.
The next hearing is scheduled for December 8, 2026.
Police issued the clarification following the renewed circulation of the video on social media.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka Police have clarified that a video circulating on social media showing a woman allegedly threatening two police officers in Gandara relates to an incident that occurred on January 28, 2024.

articles.title: Family of suspects arrested over Kavantissa shooting alleges police framed innocent men
articles.text:
Family members of suspects arrested in connection with the shooting of iconic tusker Kavantissa have denied their involvement, accusing investigators of falsely implicating innocent individuals and demanding an impartial investigation.
Speaking to the media, the wife of one of the suspects alleged that around 15 officers arrived at their residence at approximately 4:30 p.m. and pressured her husband to admit responsibility for shooting the elephant.
“My husband told them that he could never admit to something he had not done,” she said.
She said both she and her husband were government employees with two children and that the allegations had caused severe distress to their family.
“Social media is portraying my husband as a criminal. We are now in a situation where our family of four cannot face society,” she said.
The woman maintained that her husband had never committed such an offence, adding that the family had spent a considerable amount of money installing an electric fence to protect their property from elephants.
She also said the firearm seized by investigators was legally licensed and registered.
Meanwhile, a relative of another suspect alleged that officers from the Walana unit had arrested several individuals, including his brothers, despite their having no involvement in the shooting.
He further alleged that one of the arrested men had been assaulted while in custody and subsequently hospitalized with an ear injury. These allegations have not been independently verified.
The relative accused investigators of attempting to close the high-profile case by implicating innocent people rather than identifying those actually responsible.
He called on the government to conduct an independent investigation and ensure that those responsible for shooting Kavantissa are brought to justice.
“We also want to know who committed this crime. Those responsible must be punished, but innocent people should not be made to suffer,” he said.
The family members also referred to proceedings before the Mahawa Magistrate’s Court, claiming that investigators had failed to produce sufficient evidence connecting the suspects to the shooting.
During Monday’s (October 19) proceedings, Magistrate Anuradha Seneviratne questioned wildlife officials over the evidence against the suspects and directed investigators to present further material to court.
Two suspects were remanded until October 28.
However, the Ministry of Environment has maintained that investigations have established a connection between a main suspect and the shooting. Police have also reported recovering firearms and ammunition during the investigation.
Kavantissa, one of Sri Lanka’s iconic wild tuskers, died on October 16 after receiving treatment for a gunshot injury to its right foreleg.
articles.summary: Family members of suspects arrested in connection with the shooting of iconic tusker Kavantissa have denied their involvement, accusing investigators of falsely implicating innocent individuals and demanding an impartial investigation. The family members also referred to proceedings before the Mahawa Magistrate’s Court, claiming that investigators had failed to produce sufficient evidence connecting the suspects to the shooting.

articles.title: University of Moratuwa Gears Up for IDR 2026: Sri Lanka’s Premier Design and Innovation Conference
articles.text:
The University of Moratuwa is setting the stage for its flagship international design event, the
Integrated Design Research 2026 International Conference, scheduled to take place from October
21 to October 24, 2026, at the University premises. Held under the theme “The Creative Wave:
Imagination, Adaptation, and Change,” this year’s event brings together emerging student
designers, local creatives, academic heavyweights, and industry leaders from Sri Lanka and
overseas to explore how design intelligence adapts to modern challenges, from artificial intelligence
to circular economies and traditional craft.
Running alongside the Department of Integrated Design’s annual Undergraduate and Graduation
Exhibition, the four-day platform serves as a massive showcase of cross-disciplinary innovation.
The event kicks off on October 21 with the official opening of the Designer Gallery exhibition,
followed by the highly anticipated Space Conclave at 6:00 p.m., featuring a keynote presentation
by renowned Sri Lankan Architect Channa Daswatte on contemporary architecture and spatial
design.
The official conference inauguration begins on October 22 with global vision addresses and keynote
speeches, followed by rigorous academic paper presentations and scientific sessions exploring
design pedagogy, society, and culture. Visitors and industry partners can also experience the Product
Pavilion, graduate galleries, and Fashion and Media and Communication Exhibition galleries.
Day 3 also opens its doors wider to the community with specialized Creative Thinker Workshops
tailored for school students and external participants and will also hold the spectacular Fashion
Alley Show starting at 6:30 p.m., spotlighting innovative student designs and lifestyle trends. The
final day will witness the “Stitches that Speak” knitting workshop and the Packaging Boulevard as
well as the official closing ceremony in the afternoon.
Organized by the Department of Integrated Design of the Faculty of Architecture, IDR 2026
emphasizes the critical link between education and real-world industrial practice and aims to
position Sri Lanka as a growing regional voice for design innovation.
The exhibition areas are open for general public and industry viewing from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
between October 22 and 24, with preview access starting on the afternoon of October 21.
For more information and full schedules, visit the official IDR 2026 Portal at idresearch.uom.lk
articles.summary:
The University of Moratuwa is setting the stage for its flagship international design event, the
Integrated Design Research 2026 International Conference, scheduled to take place from October
21 to October 24, 2026, at the University premises.

articles.title: Regional bias in cricket selections? MP raises concerns over Milan & Viyaskanth
articles.text:
Minister of Sports Sunil Kumara Gamage has said that Sri Lanka’s national cricket selection process is based on players’ performances and abilities, rather than their ethnicity or regional background.
Responding to a question raised in Parliament, the Minister said an independent cricket selection committee was responsible for selecting players for the national team.
The question raised concerns over the limited opportunities given to cricketers Milan Rathnayake and Vijayakanth Viyaskanth, despite their performances.
The MP questioned why players from certain regions appeared to receive greater opportunities, claiming that the current Sri Lankan team touring Pakistan was largely dominated by players from the Western and Southern provinces.
He also questioned whether the Sports Ministry would intervene to ensure fair opportunities for talented players from other regions.
Responding, Minister Gamage said the selection committee considered several factors when choosing players and did not use ethnicity or geographical background as selection criteria.
“I don’t think the selection committee considers ethnicity or regional background when selecting players. They consider the abilities of the players,” the Minister said.
He added that the Ministry could bring the concerns regarding the two cricketers to the attention of the selection committee and request that their performances be considered.
Sri Lanka Cricket’s selection committee is chaired by former cricketer Kapila Wijegunawardena, who was appointed in May 2026.

The appointments were presented on Oct. 19 at the Ministry of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Cooperative Development by Minister Wasantha Samarasinghe.
Established in 1949, the CWE operations were previously suspended and moved towards liquidation in 2023. The government subsequently decided to re-establish the institution to strengthen state intervention in supplying essential food items at fair prices.

The ministry said outstanding payments of Rs. 30 million to the employees’ welfare association had also been settled and employees’ deposits released.
The new officials were selected through interviews, with the ministry stating that the process was conducted transparently and without political interference.

articles.title: China’s third-quarter growth narrowly beats forecasts
articles.text:
China’s economy grew slightly more than expected in the third quarter, but Monday’s figures still came in at the lower end of the government’s full-year target, as the global energy shock and weak domestic demand counter surging exports.
The world’s second-largest economy has charted a diverging path in recent years, with an AI-fuelled export boom masking the impact of a persistent real estate crisis and gloomy consumer sentiment.
Gross domestic product expanded 4.5 percent in July-September, according to the National Bureau of Statistics.
The reading was an improvement on the previous quarter’s 4.3 percent expansion and just ahead of the 4.4 percent predicted in an AFP poll of economists.
Beijing is hoping for annual growth this year of 4.5-5.0 percent, its lowest goal in decades.
NBS deputy head Mao Shengyong described the international context as “complex and volatile” during a news conference following the data’s publication.
He added that domestic demand was “insufficient”.
In late September, Beijing rolled out mortgage subsidies for certain home purchases and support for infrastructure investment, seeking targeted boosts for the economy as activity flagged.
While consumer activity has been a drag this year, separate data Monday showed retail sales rose 1.1 percent last month, the fastest pace since March.
However, Zhiwei Zhang, chief economist at Pinpoint Asset Management, said economic momentum remained “subdued” in September.
“After adjusting for inflation, real retail sales barely grew compared to one year ago,” he wrote.
He added that the better-than-expected GDP numbers could dissuade the government from enacting “significant” policy shifts in the fourth quarter to achieve annual targets.
Industrial production grew 5.5 percent year-on-year in September, the NBS also said Monday, up from 5.2 percent the previous month.
That increase was “helped by strong foreign demand”, wrote Nguyen Hoang Nam of Capital Economics.
‘Rebalancing’ needed
But fixed-asset investment sank 7.2 percent during the first nine months of the year combined, the data showed.
China, the world’s largest importer of crude, is under pressure from the high cost of energy caused by the Iran war, which has stymied shipping from the oil-rich Gulf.
Higher energy prices and “protracted uncertainty and structural headwinds” led the International Monetary Fund to last week slightly downgrade its projection for China’s annual growth this year to 4.5 percent.
Economists say China’s economy must shift towards a growth model powered more by domestic consumption than traditional drivers like construction, property development and exports.
That long-awaited “rebalancing” of the Chinese economy has yet to materialise, the IMF’s Asia and Pacific department director, Krishna Srinivasan, said at a press conference in Bangkok last week.
Exports — for decades the engine of China’s economy — remain a bright spot.
Figures released last week showed a surge in overseas shipments put the country on course for another record trade surplus that would top last year’s $1.2 trillion.
That export boom has been underpinned in large part by insatiable global demand for AI-related products including computers, semiconductors and data centre equipment.
But elsewhere, China’s soaring surpluses are stoking tensions with key trading partners, including the European Union and the United States.
Talks this month between EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic and Chinese counterpart Wang Wentao ended with an agreement to limit exports of Chinese hybrid vehicles to Europe.
Many critics contend that Beijing’s extensive subsidies doled out in recent years to domestic industries have given them an unfair advantage in foreign markets.
Domestic demand woes have also exacerbated the problem, as manufacturers increasingly look overseas for new growth. (France24)
articles.summary: China’s economy grew slightly more than expected in the third quarter, but Monday’s figures still came in at the lower end of the government’s full-year target, as the global energy shock and weak domestic demand counter surging exports.

articles.title: Substandard coal imports linked to Rs. 18.3 billion loss, Parliament told
articles.text:
Sri Lanka incurred an estimated Rs. 18.3 billion in losses and additional costs linked to substandard coal imports and shipment delays, S. M. Marikkar, Chairman of the Sectoral Oversight Committee on Infrastructure and Strategic Development told Parliament today.
The report, based on an investigation by an expert committee headed by the Additional Secretary to the Ministry of Energy, examined coal procurement procedures, quality discrepancies and their financial impact on electricity generation.
The findings attributed Rs. 7.099 billion to the use of substandard coal and Rs. 8.572 billion to additional electricity purchases because the required 300 megawatts of power generation was not achieved.
Other costs included additional maintenance, ash transportation and emergency coal procurement due to shipment delays, Marikkar said.
Marikkar also noted that the estimated Rs. 18.3 billion impact did not include costs associated with rising global energy prices or government subsidies provided locally. He added that the committee was instructed to make note of these costs as well.

articles.title: Foreign Minister concludes official visit to Azerbaijan
articles.text:
Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism Minister Vijitha Herath has concluded a two-day official visit to Baku, Azerbaijan, where he led Sri Lanka’s delegation to the seventh Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA).
Held on Oct. 15 under Azerbaijan’s chairmanship, the summit brought together representatives of the 28 member states to discuss regional connectivity, digitalisation and sustainable development.
Addressing the summit, Herath highlighted the importance of economic integration through stronger connectivity, digital transformation and cooperation among member states. The meeting concluded with the adoption of the Baku Declaration, the admission of Laos as a full member, the extension of Azerbaijan’s chairmanship for 2026-2028 and the appointment of Sultan Hajiyev as CICA secretary-general.
During the visit, Herath met Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev at Zuğulba Palace and held bilateral discussions with counterparts from Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Tajikistan, Turkey and Palestine, as well as CICA Secretary-General Kairat Sarybay. Discussions focused on cooperation in trade, tourism, agriculture and energy security.
He also attended a high-level business meeting with Azerbaijani energy company SOCAR to explore opportunities for energy cooperation.
Sri Lanka’s Ambassador to Iran, with accreditation to Azerbaijan, Prof. Fazeeha Azmi, and Ministry Director General for South East Asia and Central Asia Chamari Rodrigo accompanied the minister.
The Foreign Ministry said the visit reaffirmed Sri Lanka’s commitment to strengthening cooperation with CICA member states and advancing regional economic ties.

articles.title: India to slash prices of 137 cancer medicines by up to 70%
articles.text:
India has announced measures to reduce the prices of 137 cancer medicines by up to 70%, in a move aimed at making cancer treatment more affordable for patients.
The new pricing regulations will take effect on November 9, 2026, following a decision by India’s National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) to cap trade margins on the selected medicines at 30%.
According to India’s Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, the decision is expected to significantly reduce the financial burden on cancer patients and their families.
The medicines covered include treatments for more than 20 types of cancer, including breast, prostate, colon, ovarian and cervical cancers.
Several widely used cancer treatments, including pembrolizumab, bevacizumab, durvalumab and osimertinib, are among the medicines covered by the new regulations.
Pharmaceutical manufacturers have been instructed to submit revised prices within seven days of the official notification, while hospitals and pharmacies must implement the reduced prices from November 9.
Authorities have also directed pharmaceutical companies to maintain existing production and supply levels to prevent shortages.
The latest decision follows a similar initiative introduced in 2019, when India capped trade margins on 42 cancer medicines, resulting in price reductions of up to 90% across 526 brands.
The government said the latest intervention is intended to improve access to cancer treatment while preventing excessive profit margins in the pharmaceutical distribution and retail sectors.
However, the actual price reduction will vary depending on the existing pricing structure of each medicine.

The latest decision follows a similar initiative introduced in 2019, when India capped trade margins on 42 cancer medicines, resulting in price reductions of up to 90% across 526 brands.

articles.title: Tusker Kavanthissa shot by SLPP member – State Media
articles.text:
Sri Lankan state media have reported that a suspect arrested in connection with the shooting of iconic wild tusker Kavantissa is affiliated with the Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP).
According to the state-owned Dinamina newspaper, the suspect is a member of an SLPP-affiliated cooperative development body. The Sri Lanka Rupavahini Corporation, the country’s state television broadcaster, has also reported the suspect’s alleged political affiliation.
The reports come as investigations continue into the shooting of Kavantissa, whose death on October 16 sparked widespread public concern.
Two suspects arrested in connection with the shooting were remanded until October 28 after being produced before the Mahawa Magistrate’s Court on Monday (19).
Mahawa Magistrate Anuradha Seneviratne ordered wildlife officials to submit a detailed report at the next hearing, including specific evidence linking the suspects to the shooting, the date of the alleged offence and any available scientific or eyewitness evidence.
During the proceedings, wildlife officials informed the court that one suspect possessed a licensed firearm and was suspected of using it to shoot Kavantissa.
However, lawyers representing the suspects rejected the allegations, arguing that no scientific evidence had been presented to establish their clients’ involvement.
The magistrate questioned wildlife officials about the evidence supporting the shooting allegations and stressed that suspects could not be kept in remand indefinitely without sufficient supporting material.

articles.title: Akurana accident: Police reveal new details, investigate driver’s brake failure claim
articles.text:
Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) in charge of Traffic Control and Road Safety, W.P.J. Senadheera, has revealed further details about the fatal accident in Akurana, confirming that investigators are examining claims of brake failure and possible driver fatigue.
The DIG said the cement-laden truck was travelling towards Kandy from Alawathugoda when the driver reportedly lost control while negotiating a left-hand bend near Kurugoda Junction on Monday (Oct. 19).
The truck initially struck a motorcycle and dragged it for approximately 160 metres before colliding with four three-wheelers and two other vehicles.
“The driver claims that the brakes failed and that he was unable to control the vehicle. We are conducting a full investigation to establish whether this was actually the cause of the accident,” DIG Senadheera said.
He confirmed that the driver had undergone an alcohol test, which returned a negative result.
“The driver was not under the influence of alcohol. However, arrangements have been made to subject him to a drug test,” he said.
The DIG said police were also investigating whether the accident could have been caused by the driver falling asleep at the wheel.
A motor vehicle examiner’s report and a Government Analyst’s report will be obtained to establish whether a mechanical defect contributed to the collision.
DIG Senadheera stressed that drivers have a legal responsibility to ensure their vehicles are roadworthy before beginning a journey.
“Before taking a vehicle onto the road, the driver must check its brakes, lights and other essential components. The driver also has a legal responsibility in this regard,” he said.
He further revealed that authorities are preparing to introduce mandatory vehicle fitness certification every three months or after travelling 5,000 kilometres under proposed regulations.
The DIG said the truck driver would be produced before court under relevant criminal and motor traffic laws following the necessary investigations.
The accident claimed four lives and left several others injured.

Senadheera, has revealed further details about the fatal accident in Akurana, confirming that investigators are examining claims of brake failure and possible driver fatigue. articles.title: Tri-Series opener – Sri Lanka, Pakistan fined by ICC

Sri Lanka were fined 5% of their match fees, while Pakistan received a 10% fine.
According to the ICC, Sri Lanka were ruled to be one over short of the required target, while Pakistan were found to be two overs short after time allowances were taken into consideration.
Under the ICC Code of Conduct, players are fined 5% of their match fees for every over their team fails to bowl within the allotted time.
Jeff Crowe of the ICC Elite Panel of Match Referees imposed the sanctions.
Pakistan captain Shaheen Shah Afridi and Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis pleaded guilty and accepted the penalties, avoiding the need for formal hearings.
The charges were levelled by on-field umpires Asif Yaqoob and Wayne Knights, third umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid and fourth umpire Faisal Afridi.

articles.title: Nepal seeks to recover embassy land in Colombo allegedly sold without authorisation 32 years ago
articles.text:
The Nepalese government has initiated steps to recover land in Colombo that was allegedly sold to private individuals by its former honorary consul without government authorisation more than three decades ago.
According to Nepalese news outlet Onlinekhabar, Nepal purchased 1.5 acres of land in Rajagiriya, Colombo, on May 18, 1989, for US$360,000 to establish an embassy.
However, one acre of the property was reportedly sold in two successive transactions, in 1990 and 1994, by Nepal’s then honorary consul general in Sri Lanka, Albert Edirisinghe, who has since died.
Nepal’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs informed Parliament that it had found no documentation authorising the former honorary consul to sell the property.
According to the report, the land was first sold in September 1990 for US$100,000 and subsequently transferred to another individual in May 1994 for US$120,000.
The alleged unauthorised transactions remained undiscovered for more than three decades.
Nepalese authorities became aware of the issue only on June 5, 2025, while attempting to clear and fence the property.
The matter was subsequently brought to the attention of Sri Lanka’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and an investigation was launched.
Nepalese lawmaker Nishkal Rai has estimated the property’s current value at approximately US$6.5 million.
The report said Sri Lankan authorities had advised the Nepalese diplomatic mission to take measures to secure the property and establish ownership.
Nepal is continuing discussions with Sri Lankan authorities to recover the land, while investigations into the alleged unauthorised transfers remain ongoing.

articles.title: President appoints expert committee to probe Tusker ‘Kavanthissa’ death
articles.text:
President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed an expert committee to investigate all aspects surrounding the death of the tusker ‘Kavanthissa’ in the Siyambalangamuwa area of Galgamuwa on or around October 16.
The committee is tasked with examining the immediate and underlying causes of the tusker’s death, determining whether any lapses or negligence occurred during its treatment, developing standard operating procedures for wild elephant welfare and formulating recommendations for a national elephant conservation programme.
The committee is chaired by former Ministry Secretary A. H. Sarath Wijesinghe, with Professor T. Saminda Fernando, Professor A. G. Anil Pushpakumara, Professor U. K. Kalinga Padmalal, Dr. Jagath Gunawardena and Attorney-at-Law Charaka Jayaratne serving as members.
Additional Secretary to the President W. W. Harrison will serve as the committee’s coordinator. The panel is authorised to consult local and international experts and is expected to submit its comprehensive report and recommendations to the President within 30 days.
articles.summary: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed an expert committee to investigate all aspects surrounding the death of the tusker ‘Kavanthissa’ in the Siyambalangamuwa area of Galgamuwa on or around October 16.

articles.title: Foreign Ministry rejects UNP allegations over Thai Deputy PM’s Sri Lanka visit
articles.text:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has clarified that Thai Deputy Prime Minister Suphajee Suthumpun’s recent visit to Sri Lanka was entirely private and that all requested courtesies were extended by the Sri Lankan authorities.
The clarification follows allegations by the United National Party (UNP) that the Government had failed to provide appropriate diplomatic recognition and security arrangements during her visit to Mihintale.
The Foreign Ministry’s spokesperson, who also serves as Director General of Public Diplomacy, said the Thai Deputy Prime Minister visited Sri Lanka exclusively to participate in the religious enshrinement ceremony at Mihintale alongside Buddhist devotees.
The Ministry said no other government officials accompanied her in the delegation, as the visit was undertaken in a private capacity.
According to the Ministry, the Thai Embassy had requested access to the VIP lounge and other courtesies, which were granted by the Sri Lankan authorities.
The Ministry further noted that the Thai Deputy Prime Minister had previously undertaken similar private visits to Sri Lanka to participate in religious activities.
The clarification comes after the UNP called on the Government to explain why the visiting Deputy Prime Minister had allegedly not received appropriate diplomatic courtesies and security arrangements.
The Foreign Ministry maintained that the courtesies requested by the Thai side had been provided.
articles.summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has clarified that Thai Deputy Prime Minister Suphajee Suthumpun’s recent visit to Sri Lanka was entirely private and that all requested courtesies were extended by the Sri Lankan authorities.

articles.title: Bangladesh says it was not informed of its citizens’ execution by Saudi Arabia
articles.text:
Bangladesh has raised concerns with Saudi Arabia after two of its nationals were executed in Mecca without prior notification to Bangladeshi authorities.
A Bangladeshi man and woman were executed on October 14 after being convicted of committing an alleged “indecent act” inside a mosque, according to Saudi Arabia’s Interior Ministry.
However, Bangladeshi authorities said they learned of the executions only after they had taken place, raising questions about the lack of advance communication from Saudi officials.
Bangladesh’s State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Shama Obaed Islam, said the government had sought an explanation from Saudi Arabia regarding the offences and the legal proceedings that led to the death sentences.
Saudi authorities have not publicly specified the exact nature of the alleged offence.
According to media reports, the two individuals had appeared on a list of Bangladeshi prisoners provided by Saudi Arabia to the Bangladesh Consulate General in Jeddah. However, the list reportedly did not indicate that they had been sentenced to death.
The executions have sparked concern in Bangladesh, where questions have been raised over why the government was not informed before the sentences were carried out.
More than three million Bangladeshis live and work in Saudi Arabia.
The Bangladesh Foreign Ministry also raised the matter directly with the Saudi ambassador in Dhaka on October 18, seeking clarification on why its officials were not informed of the proceedings or executions.
According to Bangladeshi media reports, Saudi Arabia had previously shared a list of prisoners that included the two individuals, but the list did not disclose their death sentences.
Saudi Arabia carried out the executions under ta’zir, a category of punishment under Islamic law in which judges have discretion to determine penalties.
The case comes days after Saudi Arabia’s Supreme Court overturned a death sentence imposed on Sri Lankan national Anojan Sivarasa over a social media comment following diplomatic and legal intervention by Sri Lankan authorities.
Bangladesh says it is awaiting a detailed response from Saudi Arabia before determining its next steps, including arrangements for repatriating the bodies.
articles.summary: Bangladesh has raised concerns with Saudi Arabia after two of its nationals were executed in Mecca without prior notification to Bangladeshi authorities. According to media reports, the two individuals had appeared on a list of Bangladeshi prisoners provided by Saudi Arabia to the Bangladesh Consulate General in Jeddah.

articles.title: From books to hidden packages: Customs exposes Rs. 67.5 million drug haul
articles.text:
Officers from the Narcotics Control Unit (NCU) of Sri Lanka Customs intercepted a major consignment of illegal narcotics valued at over Rs. 67.53 million during a special operation conducted at the Central Mail Exchange in Colombo today (Oct. 19).
The seized contraband was discovered concealed within 11 suspicious international postal parcels dispatched from several countries, including Thailand, the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Belgium, France, the Netherlands and Germany. Customs officers had identified and held the suspicious parcels over recent months while monitoring incoming foreign mail, waiting for the designated recipients to claim them. After no recipients arrived within the permitted timeframe, officials opened and inspected the packages in the presence of officers from the Police Narcotic Bureau (PNB).
A full inspection revealed over 3.1 kilograms of Kush cannabis valued at over Rs. 30.5 million imported from Thailand, the United States, and the United Kingdom. Officers also confiscated 2,395 grams of MDMA (Ecstasy) pills sent from Belgium, France, Canada, and Germany, alongside 33 grams of Mandy (powdered/crystal MDMA) sent from the Netherlands. The largest single haul was contained in a parcel from Belgium, which held 2,202 grams of MDMA pills estimated at Rs. 33.03 million. Following initial inspections at the Central Mail Exchange, Sri Lanka Customs handed the seized drug consignment over to the Police Narcotic Bureau for further legal action and investigations.
articles.summary: Officers from the Narcotics Control Unit (NCU) of Sri Lanka Customs intercepted a major consignment of illegal narcotics valued at over Rs. 67.53 million during a special operation conducted at the Central Mail Exchange in Colombo today (Oct. 19). The largest single haul was contained in a parcel from Belgium, which held 2,202 grams of MDMA pills estimated at Rs. 33.03 million.

articles.title: Sri Lanka opens first Chinese yuan clearing bank in Colombo
articles.text:
Sri Lanka officially launched its Chinese Renminbi (RMB) Clearing Bank in Colombo on October 15, aiming to facilitate cross-border financial transactions and strengthen bilateral economic cooperation between Sri Lanka and China.
The ceremony was held with the participation of Minister of Labour and Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Dr. Anil Jayantha. Under authorisation from the People’s Bank of China, the Colombo branch of the Bank of China will serve as the official RMB clearing bank. The new facility enables direct cross-border RMB clearing and domestic interbank transactions, establishing direct connections between Sri Lanka’s banking network and China’s financial system.
By allowing direct settlement in Chinese Yuan, the initiative eliminates the need to convert Sri Lankan Rupees into US Dollars before converting to Yuan for trade with China. This shift is expected to reduce currency conversion costs, mitigate exchange rate risks, accelerate transaction processing times, and provide streamlined financial services for importers and exporters. The launch event was attended by Chinese Ambassador to Sri Lanka Wei Huaxiang, Bank of China Vice President and Executive Director Zhang Hui, Central Bank of Sri Lanka Deputy Governor K.G.P. Sirikumara, along with representatives from the Sri Lankan and Chinese business communities.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka officially launched its Chinese Renminbi (RMB) Clearing Bank in Colombo on October 15, aiming to facilitate cross-border financial transactions and strengthen bilateral economic cooperation between Sri Lanka and China. Under authorisation from the People’s Bank of China, the Colombo branch of the Bank of China will serve as the official RMB clearing bank.

articles.title: Suspect arrested in Tissamaharama with elephant ivory jewellery
articles.text:
A 46-year-old suspect was arrested by wildlife officers in Tissamaharama on October 16 for unlawful possession of jewellery crafted from elephant ivory.
The raid was conducted by wildlife officials following information received by the Park Warden of the Udawalawe National Park. During the operation, officers seized two ivory bangles and two ivory pendants from the suspect’s possession. Under the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance, the possession, display, transport, or sale of parts from strictly protected wild animals is prohibited by law.
The suspect and the confiscated items were produced before the Tissamaharama Magistrate’s Court on October 16. The court released the suspect on two personal bails of Rs. 100,000 each, and scheduled the next court hearing for November 20. ( Newswire)

articles.title: UK to fine bus passengers up to £100 for playing loud music
articles.text:
The UK government has announced a nationwide crackdown on public transport antisocial behaviour, under which bus passengers in England who play loud music could face fixed penalty fines of up to £100.
The proposed measures seek to address issues such as playing loud audio, littering, vaping, and threatening behaviour across public transport systems. Under newly introduced guidance, local authorities in England are being granted powers to impose penalties on bus offenders, subject to final approval by the Transport Secretary. Enforcement on buses will be handled by authorized personnel, including Transport Safety Officers and police officers, rather than bus drivers.
Alongside bus measures, the government is launching a national awareness campaign titled “share the carriage, not the noise” to remind rail passengers of existing laws against playing loud music and singing, which carry fines of up to £1,000 or removal from trains for non-compliance. While transport campaigners and public surveys indicate widespread disapproval of loudcasting, questions remain regarding how authorities will effectively enforce the new rules in practice.
articles.summary: The UK government has announced a nationwide crackdown on public transport antisocial behaviour, under which bus passengers in England who play loud music could face fixed penalty fines of up to £100.

articles.title: PUCSL approves one-hour power cuts for 3 days: Schedule released
articles.text:
The Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) has granted approval to implement one-hour power cuts across the country for three consecutive days, from today (19) until Wednesday (21).
Accordingly, the country has been divided into four groups, with each group scheduled to experience a one-hour power interruption daily between 4.30 p.m. and 9.00 p.m.
The approved demand management schedules have been released for October 19, 20 and 21, outlining the power interruption periods for each group.
For today (19), Group 1 will experience a one-hour power cut beginning between 4.30 p.m. and 5.00 p.m., Group 2 between 5.30 p.m. and 6.00 p.m., Group 3 between 6.30 p.m. and 7.00 p.m., and Group 4 between 7.30 p.m. and 8.00 p.m.
For tomorrow (20), Group 4 will experience a one-hour power cut beginning between 4.30 p.m. and 5.00 p.m., Group 1 between 5.30 p.m. and 6.00 p.m., Group 2 between 6.30 p.m. and 7.00 p.m., and Group 3 between 7.30 p.m. and 8.00 p.m.
On Wednesday (21), Group 3 will experience a one-hour power cut beginning between 4.30 p.m. and 5.00 p.m., Group 4 between 5.30 p.m. and 6.00 p.m., Group 1 between 6.30 p.m. and 7.00 p.m., and Group 2 between 7.30 p.m. and 8.00 p.m.
According to the schedules, the power cuts will be implemented if the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) is required to manage electricity demand due to insufficient generation capacity resulting from the unavailability of the Lakvijaya Power Station following a blackout.
The authorities stated that the interruption and restoration times may vary by up to 30 minutes, depending on electricity demand, available generation capacity and prevailing weather conditions.
Earlier today, National System Operator (NSO) Company Chief Executive Officer Buddhika Samarasinghe announced that approval had been sought from the PUCSL to implement one-hour power cuts from October 19 to 21.
articles.summary: The Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) has granted approval to implement one-hour power cuts across the country for three consecutive days, from today (19) until Wednesday (21).

articles.title: Sri Lanka promotes mineral resources and investment opportunities in Japan
articles.text:
Sri Lanka has stepped up efforts to attract Japanese investment into its mineral sector, with a high-level delegation led by Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Sunil Handunnetthi visiting Japan to explore investment opportunities, technology transfer and value-added production.
According to the Sri Lankan Embassy in Tokyo, the Minister led a delegation of senior government officials and private-sector representatives to Japan from October 13 to 16.
As part of the visit, the Sri Lanka–Japan Mineral Sector Promotion Seminar and Investor Roundtable Discussion was held at the headquarters of the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) in Tokyo on October 14.
The event, jointly organised by the Sri Lankan Embassy and JETRO, attracted more than 100 participants and highlighted investment opportunities in Sri Lanka’s mineral sector.
Ten Sri Lankan companies showcased their products and investment opportunities, followed by business discussions with Japanese stakeholders.
The discussions focused on potential cooperation in graphite, mineral sands, quartz and other mineral resources, with particular attention to mineral processing, resource assessment, value addition and strengthening supply chains.
The Embassy stated that this was the first time the Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development had organised a delegation to Japan specifically to promote a single economic sector.
The initiative forms part of efforts to develop the mineral sector as a priority under Sri Lanka’s National Export Development Programme and contribute towards the country’s target of achieving US$36 billion in exports by 2030.
During the visit, Minister Handunnetthi and the delegation also held discussions with senior representatives of several Japanese institutions, including JETRO, the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), the Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security (JOGMEC) and Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry.
Meetings were also held with Japanese government representatives to explore cooperation in geological surveys, technical capacity building, mineral processing and investment promotion.
According to the Embassy, the visit was aimed at strengthening Sri Lanka–Japan economic relations, attracting new investments and supporting Sri Lanka’s export diversification and long-term economic development.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka has stepped up efforts to attract Japanese investment into its mineral sector, with a high-level delegation led by Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Sunil Handunnetthi visiting Japan to explore investment opportunities, technology transfer and value-added production. The event, jointly organised by the Sri Lankan Embassy and JETRO, attracted more than 100 participants and highlighted investment opportunities in Sri Lanka’s mineral sector.

The Colombo Crime Division (CCD) has recorded a statement from Ven. Ulapane Sumangala Thera in connection with an investigation into allegations that Ven. Balangoda Kassapa Thera was assaulted by police officers during a recent protest.
According to Police, officers of the CCD visited the school where Ven. Ulapane Sumangala Thera serves and recorded a statement from him for nearly three hours on Monday (19).
The investigation follows claims circulated through mainstream and social media alleging that Ven. Balangoda Kassapa Thera was assaulted by police during a protest demanding the immediate release of Bodu Bala Sena (BBS) General Secretary Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera, who is currently serving a prison sentence for contempt of court.
Police stated that no formal complaint regarding the alleged assault on Ven. Balangoda Kassapa Thera has been lodged at any police station so far.
However, following the circulation of the allegations, the Acting Inspector General of Police instructed the CCD to launch an immediate investigation.
The investigation aims to establish whether any police officers had assaulted the monk during the protest.
Further investigations are underway.

articles.title: UNP questions Govt’s foreign policy over alleged Thai Deputy PM protocol lapse
articles.text:
The United National Party (UNP) has called on the Government to provide an immediate clarification over the alleged failure to extend a diplomatic reception and security to Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister Suphajee Suthumpun during her recent visit to Sri Lanka.
In a statement issued today (19), the UNP questioned why the Thai Deputy Prime Minister had allegedly not been accorded diplomatic protocol or security arrangements during her visit to attend the ceremonial unveiling of the pinnacle of the Mihindu Maha Seya in Mihintale.
The party claimed that the incident reflected the shortcomings of the National People’s Power (NPP) Government’s foreign policy.
According to the UNP, it is customary for Sri Lanka to extend diplomatic courtesies and security arrangements to visiting foreign leaders, irrespective of whether their visits are official or private.
The party cited the example of former British Prime Minister David Cameron, who was reportedly provided special security during a private visit to Sri Lanka after leaving office.
The UNP further pointed out that Suphajee Suthumpun had attended the religious ceremony as its chief guest in her official capacity as Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister.
Highlighting the longstanding diplomatic and religious ties between Sri Lanka and Thailand, the party said the Thai Deputy Prime Minister had also facilitated the bringing of the pinnacle structure and crest gem from Thailand for the ceremony.
The UNP called on the Minister of Buddhasasana and Religious Affairs to explain why the visiting Deputy Prime Minister had allegedly not been accorded appropriate diplomatic recognition and security.
articles.summary: The United National Party (UNP) has called on the Government to provide an immediate clarification over the alleged failure to extend a diplomatic reception and security to Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister Suphajee Suthumpun during her recent visit to Sri Lanka.

articles.title: Weather alert: Heavy rains expected across Sri Lanka from Tuesday evening
articles.text:
Showery conditions across Sri Lanka are expected to intensify from the evening of Tuesday, October 20, due to the development of an atmospheric disturbance in the lower atmosphere near the island, the Department of Meteorology warned.
In its 36-hour weather forecast issued at 4 p.m. on October 19, the department said showers or thundershowers are expected in most parts of the country after 1 p.m.
Fairly heavy rainfall exceeding 75 mm is likely in some areas of the Northern, North Central, Central and Uva provinces, as well as Trincomalee district.
Morning showers are also expected in coastal areas of the Western and Northern provinces and Puttalam district.
The department warned of temporary strong winds and lightning during thundershowers, urging the public to take necessary precautions.
Misty conditions are also expected in parts of the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central and Uva provinces during the early morning hours.

articles.title: Speaker endorses Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Bill
articles.text:
Speaker of Parliament Jagath Wickramaratne has endorsed the certificate on the Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Bill today (19), bringing the legislation into law.
According to a Parliament statement, the Bill has been enacted as the Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Act, No. 25 of 2026.
The Bill was initially presented to Parliament for its First Reading on August 19, 2026, by Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya.
The Second Reading debate was held on October 8, following which the Bill was passed with amendments, without a division.
The new legislation seeks to address legal, interpretative, administrative and technical issues identified during the implementation of the Anti-Corruption Act, No. 9 of 2023.
It also aims to resolve inconsistencies between the Sinhala and English versions of the Act and address challenges relating to the investigation and prosecution of corruption offences.
Additionally, the amendments are intended to improve the administrative functions of the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) and streamline the submission of assets and liabilities declarations through a centralized electronic system.
According to Parliament, the amendments are expected to strengthen Sri Lanka’s legal and institutional framework for combating corruption while ensuring greater transparency, accountability and effective implementation of anti-corruption laws.
articles.summary: Speaker of Parliament Jagath Wickramaratne has endorsed the certificate on the Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Bill today (19), bringing the legislation into law. According to a Parliament statement, the Bill has been enacted as the Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Act, No. 25 of 2026.

articles.title: Minor Hotels Sri Lanka Announces Leadership Promotions Across Its Kalutara Resort Complex
articles.text:
Minor Hotels Sri Lanka has announced two leadership promotions across its Kalutara resort complex, comprising Anantara Kalutara Resort and Avani Kalutara Resort. Jude Silva, previously Hotel Manager at Avani Kalutara Resort, has been promoted to Complex Resort Manager, while Ashane Fernando, formerly Cluster Assistant Director of Sales, has been promoted to Complex Director of Operations. Both appointments encompass Anantara Kalutara Resort and Avani Kalutara Resort, bringing together extensive resort management experience and a strong understanding of hospitality operations and commercial performance.
The promotions celebrate two distinct career journeys rooted in hands-on guest service and shaped by continuous learning. Together, Jude Silva and Ashane Fernando bring perspectives that will support the teams across both properties in delivering thoughtful service, strengthening operational standards and creating memorable stays that reflect each brand’s individual character.
Jude’s hospitality career began in the early 1980s in housekeeping, laying the foundation for decades of growth into resort leadership. His experience spans Villa Ocean View, Hotel Sigiriya and Hibiscus Hotel, followed by his role as Executive Housekeeper at Hotel Serendib in Bentota, where he strengthened his operational expertise and people management skills.
In 2009, a cross-exposure placement at Anantara Hua Hin Resort in Thailand, facilitated by Serendib Leisure Management, broadened his understanding of international luxury hospitality and Anantara’s service culture. He later assumed wider management responsibilities at Club Hotel Dolphin before joining Avani Kalutara Resort as Resident Manager and progressing to Resort Manager.
His promotion to Complex Resort Manager recognises a career shaped by perseverance, continuous learning and a commitment to people, bringing extensive operational knowledge and thoughtful.
Ashane began his career as a Front Office Trainee at Cinnamon Red Colombo, gaining an understanding of guest service before moving into sales. Over more than eight years with Cinnamon Hotels & Resorts, he progressed through sales and commercial roles across city and resort properties. His final position with the group was Senior Manager – Sales at Cinnamon Bentota Beach, where he contributed to the resort’s transition into Cinnamon’s luxury Signature Selection.
In March 2025, Ashane joined Minor Hotels Sri Lanka as Cluster Assistant Director of Sales, overseeing meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE), leisure and corporate business across the Sri Lankan portfolio. His responsibilities spanned corporate accounts, weddings, group business and destination sales, further developing his understanding of how commercial strategy translates into guest expectations and hotel performance.
Appointed Complex Director of Operations in September 2026, Ashane now brings that commercial perspective to the delivery of the guest experience across both Kalutara resorts. The move builds on his front office beginnings, connecting his knowledge of markets and client needs with the daily work of resort teams. His focus is on aligning the experiences promised to guests with the service they receive, while supporting team development and long-term business growth.
Set between the Indian Ocean and the Kalu Ganga lagoon on Sri Lanka’s west coast, Anantara Kalutara Resort and Avani Kalutara Resort form a distinctive coastal resort complex within convenient reach of Colombo. The neighbouring Minor Hotels properties bring two complementary hospitality experiences into one destination: Anantara’s personalised luxury and sense of place, alongside Avani’s relaxed style and lively social atmosphere.
Across the complex, guests can shape their stay around private pool villa residences, Geoffrey Bawa-inspired architecture, distinctive dining, spa and Ayurvedic wellness experiences, or family recreation and adventure. Lagoon water sports, kayaking and activities at the Glider Adventure Tower add an active dimension to a coastal escape, while wedding and meeting facilities extend the destination’s appeal to celebrations and business gatherings. This breadth gives couples, families and groups the freedom to combine relaxation, discovery and shared experiences within one Kalutara setting.
As Jude and Ashane step into their expanded roles, their journeys offer an encouraging example of the opportunities hospitality creates for those who continue to learn and grow. Their combined experience will help guide the next chapter for Anantara Kalutara Resort and Avani Kalutara Resort, with the people behind each guest experience at the heart of their leadership.
articles.summary: Minor Hotels Sri Lanka has announced two leadership promotions across its Kalutara resort complex, comprising Anantara Kalutara Resort and Avani Kalutara Resort. Jude Silva, previously Hotel Manager at Avani Kalutara Resort, has been promoted to Complex Resort Manager, while Ashane Fernando, formerly Cluster Assistant Director of Sales, has been promoted to Complex Director of Operations.

articles.title: SLPA confirms cancellation of USD 280 million Chinese-backed Colombo Port logistics project
articles.text:
The Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) has confirmed that the proposed USD 280 million logistics project at the Port of Colombo will not proceed, following an earlier announcement by the Chinese company involved in the joint venture.
In a statement issued today (19), the SLPA said the shareholders of South Asia Commercial and Logistics Hub (SACLH) had decided not to proceed with the project following a review of external circumstances, commercial considerations and their respective interests.
Established in 2023, the joint venture involved China Merchants Port Holdings Company Limited, through its wholly owned subsidiary, with a 70% stake, while the SLPA and Access Engineering PLC each held 15%.
The project was originally planned as a modern logistics facility with an investment of approximately USD 280 million and a floor capacity of 150,000 square metres.
The SLPA confirmed that approximately USD 29.8 million in equity contributions would be refunded to the three shareholders in proportion to their stakes, subject to regulatory requirements and operational expenses.
However, the Authority announced plans to develop a new logistics hub at the Port of Colombo through a Public–Private Partnership (PPP) model, with investors to be selected through a competitive bidding process.
The SLPA said the decision to discontinue the earlier joint venture would not affect its commitment to developing modern logistics infrastructure at the port.
It added that the alternative development model would aim to attract private investment, improve port efficiency and strengthen Colombo’s position as a regional maritime and logistics hub.
articles.summary: The Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) has confirmed that the proposed USD 280 million logistics project at the Port of Colombo will not proceed, following an earlier announcement by the Chinese company involved in the joint venture.

articles.title: PM vows strict enforcement of environmental laws following Kawanthissa’s death
articles.text:
Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya says the Government is deeply saddened by the death of tusker Kawanthissa, who succumbed to severe gunshot injuries despite efforts by wildlife officers and veterinary teams to save its life.
Addressing the Presidential Environmental Awards 2026 held in Colombo today (19), the Prime Minister said the tragedy must never be repeated.
She emphasised that environmental laws would be strictly enforced against those responsible for environmental crimes, irrespective of their position, wealth or connections.
“We cannot allow tragedies such as the one that befell Tusker Kawanthissa to happen again. Environmental laws must not be influenced by a person’s position, wealth or connections. The law will be enforced equally against everyone.”
The Prime Minister said wildlife officers and veterinary teams had made significant efforts to save Kawanthissa, but the elephant could not be saved due to the severity of its injuries and resulting infections.
She added that the Government would further strengthen wildlife veterinary care and veterinary education to prevent similar incidents in the future.
Highlighting measures taken to address the human-elephant conflict, the Prime Minister said 113 forest areas covering approximately 71,900 hectares had been designated as reserves.
She said three elephant corridors were also being established to facilitate the movement of elephants, alongside a dedicated elephant management reserve.
To strengthen the Department of Wildlife Conservation, the Government has provided 100 pickup vehicles, 185 motorcycles and nine tractors, while 3,500 elephant fence assistants and 5,000 Civil Security Department personnel have been deployed to maintain elephant fences.
The Prime Minister also announced that steps had been taken to amend the National Environmental Act after 26 years, while more than 1,600 new officers were being recruited to the Ministry of Environment.
Emphasising the importance of sustainable development, she said environmental protection must be incorporated into government policy and the daily lives of citizens.
“Development achieved at the expense of environmental destruction can never be considered sustainable development.”
articles.summary: Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya says the Government is deeply saddened by the death of tusker Kawanthissa, who succumbed to severe gunshot injuries despite efforts by wildlife officers and veterinary teams to save its life. She emphasised that environmental laws would be strictly enforced against those responsible for environmental crimes, irrespective of their position, wealth or connections.

articles.title: October 20: ‘Caution level’ heat alert issued for 14 districts
articles.text:
The Department of Meteorology has issued a ‘Caution level’ heat advisory for 14 districts across Sri Lanka, valid for tomorrow (20).
According to the advisory issued today (19), the heat index, which indicates the temperature felt on the human body, is expected to rise to ‘Caution level’ in some areas of the Northern, North-Central, Eastern and North-Western provinces, as well as the Monaragala and Hambantota districts.
The Met Department stated that a ‘Caution level’ heat index, ranging from 39°C to 45°C, could cause fatigue during prolonged exposure and physical activity, while continued activity could result in heat cramps.
The public has been advised to remain hydrated, take frequent breaks in shaded areas and limit strenuous outdoor activities.
People are also encouraged to wear lightweight, light-coloured clothing, check on elderly and sick individuals and avoid leaving children unattended inside vehicles.
articles.summary: The Department of Meteorology has issued a ‘Caution level’ heat advisory for 14 districts across Sri Lanka, valid for tomorrow (20).
