articles.title: Pragyan Ojha replaces Ajit Agarkar as India’s chief selector
articles.text:
Former Indian spinner Pragyan Ojha has been named Chairman of India’s Men’s Selection Committee, replacing Ajit Agarkar, the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) announced on October 19.
The BCCI also confirmed the appointment of former India spinner Ramesh Powar to the selection committee following interviews conducted by its Cricket Advisory Committee.
Ojha will chair the five-member panel based on seniority, determined by the number of Test matches played.
The new selection committee comprises Pragyan Ojha (Chairperson), Shiv Sundar Das, RP Singh, Ajay Ratra and Ramesh Powar.
Powar represented India in two Tests and 31 ODIs and previously served as head coach of India’s women’s team.
The BCCI also thanked outgoing chief selector Ajit Agarkar for his contribution since July 2023, highlighting India’s success in winning three ICC trophies, two Asia Cup titles and back-to-back Asian Games gold medals during his tenure.
articles.summary: Former Indian spinner Pragyan Ojha has been named Chairman of India’s Men’s Selection Committee, replacing Ajit Agarkar, the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) announced on October 19.

articles.title: Over 120 volunteers join Beira Lake restoration initiative in Colombo
articles.text:
The Asia Pacific Alliance for Disaster Management Sri Lanka (A-PAD SL) has launched its first activity under the Clean Waterways Initiative Programme, aimed at supporting the restoration of Colombo’s Beira Lake.
The programme, held on October 8 at the Sri Uttarananda Mawatha Pier, brought together more than 120 participants, including volunteers, government agencies and representatives of partner organisations.
Organised as part of an initiative of the Beira Lake Restoration Task Force, the event was conducted in partnership with HSBC Sri Lanka and Clean Ocean Force Sri Lanka.
The programme commenced with the unveiling of anti-pollution awareness placards at strategic locations around the lake, followed by a volunteer-led mapping exercise to identify areas affected by waste accumulation and pollution.
Volunteers from the Sri Jinarathana Vocational Training Centre, College of Fashion and Design, University of Colombo and University of Sri Jayewardenepura participated in the exercise.
During the activity, volunteers identified waste accumulation points along the lake’s banks and surrounding pathways, while recording observations relating to algae, odour, water inlets, waste barriers and potential areas for development.
The event was attended by representatives of Gangaramaya Temple, Sri Lanka Police, the Police Special Task Force, Sri Lanka Navy, Sri Lanka Land Development Corporation, educational institutions, non-governmental organisations and the British Council.
An A-PAD SL Search and Rescue team was also deployed on the lake to support the programme.
According to A-PAD SL, the Clean Waterways Programme seeks to improve Beira Lake’s water quality while promoting its development as an important transportation and economic hub.
The initiative also aims to strengthen public awareness, environmental education and responsible waste disposal practices among communities and stakeholders surrounding the lake.
articles.summary: The Asia Pacific Alliance for Disaster Management Sri Lanka (A-PAD SL) has launched its first activity under the Clean Waterways Initiative Programme, aimed at supporting the restoration of Colombo’s Beira Lake. Organised as part of an initiative of the Beira Lake Restoration Task Force, the event was conducted in partnership with HSBC Sri Lanka and Clean Ocean Force Sri Lanka.

articles.title: Gammanpila challenges anti-terrorism Bill and court order on monks
articles.text:
Former Minister Udaya Gammanpila has filed a petition before the Supreme Court challenging certain provisions of the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill presented to Parliament by the Government.
In his petition, Gammanpila has requested the Supreme Court to declare that certain provisions of the proposed Bill are inconsistent with the Constitution.
The Attorney General has been named as the respondent in the petition.
The former Minister claims that several provisions of the proposed legislation violate fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution.
Accordingly, Gammanpila has requested the Supreme Court to rule that the disputed provisions, if they are to be enacted, must be approved by a two-thirds majority in Parliament and endorsed through a referendum.
The former minister further said that a writ petition has also been filed against the court order issued by the Fort Magistrate last Friday (16) preventing Ven. Ulapane Sumangala Thera and 54 others from remaining outside the Presidential Secretariat in Colombo.
The monks had staged a march from Kandy, calling for the release of the General Secretary of the Bodu Bala Sena (BBS), Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera, and settled down in front of the Presidential Secretariat staging a protest.
An order was issued by Colombo Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena prohibiting the monks from staying at the said location and ordering the Police to remove them from the location.
Speaking to reporters, Udaya Gammanpila said the writ petition against the Colombo Fort Magistrate’s order was filed at the Court of Appeal today.
articles.summary: Former Minister Udaya Gammanpila has filed a petition before the Supreme Court challenging certain provisions of the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill presented to Parliament by the Government. In his petition, Gammanpila has requested the Supreme Court to declare that certain provisions of the proposed Bill are inconsistent with the Constitution.

articles.title: Akurana accident: Driver arrested as death toll reaches four
articles.text:
The driver of the cement lorry involved in the multi-vehicle collision in the Akurana area today (19), which claimed four lives, has been arrested.
According to the Police, the driver was arrested by the Alawathugoda Police following the fatal accident.
The accident occurred this morning at Kurugoda Junction, near the 7th milepost in Akurana, along the Kandy–Matale A9 Road.
Police stated that a bulk tanker lorry transporting cement powder from Alawathugoda towards Kandy had reportedly gone out of the driver’s control and collided with several vehicles travelling ahead of it before overturning.
Four individuals were killed in the accident, while six others sustained serious injuries and were admitted to hospitals in Kandy and Akurana.
Alawathugoda Police are conducting further investigations into the incident.

articles.title: Microfinance loans under scrutiny over excessive interest rates
articles.text:
Sri Lanka’s Parliamentary Sectoral Oversight Committee on Economic Development and International Relations has called for the speedy implementation of the Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority Act to regulate lending institutions and protect borrowers from excessive interest rates.
The committee, chaired by MP Lakmali Hemachandra, discussed the matter during a recent meeting with representatives of the Sri Lanka Microfinance Practitioners’ Association.
According to Parliament, particular attention was given to lending institutions charging excessively high interest rates through informal practices, causing financial hardship to the public.
The committee stressed the importance of establishing a fair regulatory framework while ensuring that properly functioning microfinance institutions can continue their operations.
Discussions also focused on simplifying licensing procedures, allowing regulated microfinance institutions to accept limited public deposits under supervision and providing access to lower-cost funding.
The possibility of securing concessional funding from international institutions, including the Asian Development Bank, to help reduce lending interest rates was also considered.
The committee further examined consumer protection measures, the establishment of the proposed Regulatory Authority and deadlines for institutions to obtain licences.
Meanwhile, the committee discussed a request by state-owned Lanka Mineral Sands Limited (LMSL) seeking exclusive mining rights over 68 grids containing mineral sand deposits along Sri Lanka’s northeastern coastline.
LMSL requested that these deposits not be allocated to private institutions.
The committee also reviewed concerns over previously issued mining licences, including alleged irregularities, and noted that information relating to certain irregularities had been referred to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID).
The committee decided to issue recommendations on mining rights and operational support for LMSL, while also considering measures to strengthen transparency in future mining licence approvals.

The possibility of securing concessional funding from international institutions, including the Asian Development Bank, to help reduce lending interest rates was also considered.

articles.title: “I was misled” – Maithri apologizes, reveals what went wrong with Gnanasara Thera’s presidential pardon
articles.text:
Former President Maithripala Sirisena has claimed that officials at the Presidential Secretariat misled him during the process of granting a presidential pardon to Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera, resulting in a technical error that eventually led to the monk’s reimprisonment.
In a statement issued on October 19, Sirisena said he had studied a copy of the relevant court judgment and understood that a technical defect in documents submitted by the Presidential Secretariat had contributed to the court’s decision.
He said Gnanasara Thera had faced two cases before the Homagama Magistrate’s Court, identified as B 7417/10 and 40042.
According to Sirisena, the additional senior secretary in charge of legal affairs at the Presidential Secretariat had informed him that approval from the Ministry of Justice and Prisons was required in connection with the pardon.
However, he alleged that the necessary documents were never forwarded to the ministry and that his signature was obtained without securing the required approval.
“This was misleading me,” Sirisena said.
The former President claimed that the error committed by officials during his presidency had ultimately resulted in Gnanasara Thera being imprisoned again, following legal proceedings initiated through a complaint by Sandya Ekneligoda involving an organization associated with Paikiasothy Saravanamuttu.
Sirisena said he respected the court’s decision and accepted that the judgment was correct.
He also apologized to the Buddhist clergy for the mistake, although he maintained that it had been committed by officials serving under his administration.
The former President said he issued the statement following inquiries from Buddhist monks, journalists and members of the public seeking clarification about the technical error that affected the presidential pardon.
articles.summary: Former President Maithripala Sirisena has claimed that officials at the Presidential Secretariat misled him during the process of granting a presidential pardon to Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera, resulting in a technical error that eventually led to the monk’s reimprisonment.
